title: power-latency-p50-p99-sampling-study
content:
Summary:

This note captures an exploratory benchmarking run focused on the relationship between GPU power draw and tail latency (p50/p95/p99) across A100, H100, and L40S cloud SKUs and multiple driver/CUDA combinations. Primary goal: identify operating points (power caps, driver versions, instance SKUs) where our runtime gives the best trade-off for low-p50 latency and predictable p99 behavior for both single-tenant reserved and multi-tenant shared hosting.

Why we did this: previous runs looked at throughput and occupancy but did not explicitly correlate power throttling/thermal states with latency tail behavior under realistic mixed workloads (small chat requests + occasional long generations). We saw unexplained p99 spikes in production; hypothesized interactions between power capping, PCIe/NVLink memory transfer latency, and CUDA driver scheduler behavior.

Experiment setup (short):
- Models: 7B decoder-only (FP16), 13B decoder-only (FP16) with KV cache enabled.
- Clients: mixed synthetic workload: 70% short ctx (prompt 32 tokens, gen 32 tokens), 25% medium (128->128), 5% long (512->512). Poisson arrival to emulate burstiness.
- Runtime: Redwood serving runtime (main branch, binary built 2026-02), KV prefetch enabled, dynamic batching (max batch 32), per-request latency SLO target 150ms default.
- SKUs tested (cloud aliases):
  - AWS: p4d.24xlarge (A100-80GB NVLink), p5.48xlarge (H100 NVLink)
  - GCP: a2-megagpu-16g (A100), g5-48 (H100)
  - Azure: ND A100 v4 (A100 80GB), ND H100 v5 (H100)
- GPU configurations: stock driver (NVIDIA 525 / CUDA 11.8), newer driver (NVIDIA 535 / CUDA 12.1), experimental CUDA 12.2 dev driver (where available).
- Monitoring: Nsight Systems sampling, nvidia-smi sampling at 1s, CUPTI traces for kernel launch times (spot checks), host perf for context switches.
- Power control: where allowed, runs with (a) stock auto power, (b) explicit vendor power cap -10%, (c) +5% (where allowed), and (d) thermal constraint induced by sustained high freq workload.

Top-level observations (high level):
- H100 gives best median latency (p50) for short requests when running on H100 SKUs with CUDA 12.1 + driver 535, typically 12–18% lower p50 vs equivalent A100 SKUs under same batching policy.
- A100 tends to have more consistent p99 under heavy mixed bursts, particularly when power is capped slightly (-10%). We saw p99 reductions of ~20% on A100 when applying conservative power caps that reduced thermal throttling oscillations.
- L40S (cloud vendor variants) showed the most stable p99 across the spectrum for medium-length jobs; however p50 was typically worse than H100 by 8–15%. L40S appears optimized for sustained throughput (thermally conservative clocks) instead of short-latency bursts.
- Driver/CUDA matters: the 535/12.1 combo reduced kernel launch overhead and improved stream scheduling jitter vs 525/11.8 in H100 runs. On A100, 525/11.8 with a slight power cap produced more stable tails in our runs. CUDA 12.2 showed promise (reduced small-kernel overhead) but was only available on a subset of hosts and produced occasional increases in PCIe transfer latency on specific NIC+driver combinations (investigate).

Detailed notes and numbers (representative):
- H100 (p5-like node) with driver 535/CUDA 12.1, auto power:
  - p50 short requests: ~38ms
  - p95 short requests: ~85ms
  - p99 short requests: ~160–200ms (depends on network noise)
- A100 (p4d-like node) with driver 525/CUDA 11.8, power cap -10%:
  - p50 short: ~46ms
  - p95 short: ~92ms
  - p99 short: ~110–130ms (more consistent)
- L40S (vendor-stock) with driver 535/CUDA 12.1:
  - p50 short: ~52ms
  - p95 short: ~98ms
  - p99 short: ~115–145ms

Interpretation and root cause hypotheses: (what we think is happening)
1) Thermal oscillation and GPU boost behavior: H100 aggressively boosts to higher clocks for short bursts which lowers p50 but can cause thermal or power management subsystems to step in during sustained bursts, causing a spike in p99 (the runtime sees sudden slowdown mid-generation). A100's more conservative clock scaling (especially when slightly power-capped) avoids these oscillations.

2) Driver-level kernel dispatch jitter: newer CUDA (12.x) improved small-kernel launch amortization on H100, which helps p50. However, vendor NIC driver interactions (RDMA/CUDA memcpy async path on certain host OS kernels) can add sporadic delays for KV cache prefetchs that show up as p99. We observed correlated host CPU context switch spikes during the slow tails.

3) Multi-tenant interference: on shared instances (multi-container) we saw that small background processes (e.g., nv-peer-mem or vendor monitoring agents) can grab PCIe bandwidth or trigger host interrupts leading to 1–2s-scale p99 outliers. These are more prominent on H100 nodes in our cloud of test accounts (likely different host BIOS/firmware defaults).

4) Memory subsystem and NVLink saturation: long-context generations can saturate NVLink aggregates on A100 clusters with several concurrent models, resulting in slightly higher p50 but lower p99 compared to H100 where compute-bound short bursts dominate.

Actionable recommendations (short):
- For low-latency chat (short prompt + short gen) we prefer H100 SKUs with driver 535/CUDA 12.1 in a dedicated capacity offering but apply the following runtime heuristics:
  - Aggressive early-exit batching (batch hinting for short requests) to keep p50 low.
  - Soft CPU pinning and isolation for background host processes in the VM image; production images should disable vendor telemetry where safe.

- For mixed workloads (chat + occasional long completions) and when p99 predictability is prioritized, prefer A100 80GB SKUs with a mild static power cap (-5 to -10%) and driver 525/11.8. That combination yielded fewer tail anomalies in our runs.

- L40S: good candidate for steady throughput jobs (embedding pipelines, batch offline inference). If using L40S for chat, expect slightly higher medians but stable tails.

- Driver strategy: adopt a per-region driver matrix in Console (visible to infra) and tie recommended driver image to deployment type (latency-optimized vs throughput-optimized). Do not auto-upgrade host driver across regions without staged validation.

Operational notes and quick mitigation recipes:
- If you see sudden p99 spikes in production: check nvidia-smi power draw and host CPU steal/context switch rates; if power or thermal oscillation is visible, try a temporary soft power cap and deploy a host image with vendor telemetry disabled.
- Add a lightweight watchdog in the runtime that detects persistent drop in kernel throughput and proactively drains KV cache + swap to a slower model variant (fallback) to avoid cascading p99 spikes during thermal events.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Why does CUDA 12.2 show increased host PCIe memcpy latency on some hosts? Need a microbenchmark of cudaMemcpyAsync path with our NIC stacks (RDMA offload enabled vs disabled).
- Need to reproduce multi-tenant interference with an instrumented host and vendor BIOS settings to confirm whether it's firmware defaults or cloud scheduler packing.
- Investigate whether different NUMA bindings on multi-GPU instances affect KV prefetch latency (we saw hints on GCP a2 nodes).

Planned next experiments (brief):
- Isolate kernel launch jitter: run a focused test with 1:1 client:GPU and heavy small-kernel mix to quantify kernel launch overhead across driver versions with Nsight sampling at 10ms resolution.
- Run sustained thermal soak tests on H100 with synthetic bursts to measure the exact time-to-throttle and characterize recovery curves (use vendor telemetry + power cap sweeps).
- Run the same mixed-workload suite with and without vendor telemetry/monitoring agents to measure impact of host-side background processes.

Notes to self (todo):
- Capture raw Nsight traces and push to S3 under s3://redwood-bench/power-latency/2026-02-xx for later offline analysis.
- Create a Linear ticket to track driver rollout policy: LINEAR-2317.

Appendix: quick checklist for infra engineers prepping an image for low-latency H100 runs:
- Disable vendor telemetry agents (confirm with security).
- Pin runtime threads to dedicated cores; isolate background interrupts where possible.
- Ship driver 535 + CUDA 12.1 images for H100 latency pools; keep 525/11.8 images for A100 throughput pools until 12.2 is validated.

If you're reviewing this: please comment with any region-specific oddities you've seen (EWR vs IAD vs EMEA). Also flag if you want the raw traces or a condensed CSV of p50/p95/p99 across all runs.

-- Maya
